## 2. When Can a Google Review Be Removed? (Policy-to-Evidence Matrix)

Google only removes reviews that violate its [Prohibited and Restricted Content Policies](https://support.google.com/contributionpolicy/answer/7400114). Reviewell assesses each review against these exact criteria before accepting a case:

| Policy Violation Category | Typical Business Scenario | Required Factual Evidence for Escalation |
|---|---|---|
| **Fake Engagement / Non-Customer** | Reviewer never visited or interacted with the business; bot or paid attack. | CRM/booking logs, POS invoice timestamp audit, absence of customer record, sudden multi-account velocity spike log. |
| **Conflict of Interest** | Review left by a current/former employee, direct competitor, or affiliated party. | Employment contract/termination record, company registry (KBO/BCE) extract linking reviewer to competitor, LinkedIn/public affiliation proof. |
| **Harassment, Doxxing & Personal Data** | Review names non-public staff, shares private phone numbers, photos, or home addresses. | Screenshot highlighting personal data (GDPR Art. 17 erasure relevance), staff identity confirmation, threat/harassment report. |
| **Off-Topic / Wrong Business** | Reviewer confused the business with another company or ranted about unrelated topics. | Address/name disambiguation proof, service scope documentation showing the claimed service is not offered. |
| **Coordinated Review Bombing** | Sudden influx of 1-star ratings triggered by social media brigading or extortion. | Timeline anomaly chart, extortion message screenshots (WhatsApp/email), IP/timing cluster documentation. |

## 3. Frequently Asked Questions (Direct-Answer Format)

### Does Reviewell offer a free check before charging?
Yes. Businesses start with a **free Google review eligibility check** at `https://www.reviewell.com/#check` by sharing the review link and explaining the factual context. Reviewell evaluates whether the review plausibly breaches platform rules before any paid casework is proposed.

### Can Reviewell remove genuine negative customer reviews?
No. Genuine customer criticism and honest dissatisfaction do not violate Google's content policies and cannot be removed through policy escalation. Reviewell only pursues cases supported by factual evidence of a policy breach or unlawful content.

### How does the 5-step Reviewell process work?
1. **Free Check:** Submit the review URL and background context at `https://www.reviewell.com/#check`.
2. **Assessment:** Reviewell establishes the facts, identifies the applicable Google policy route, and lists required evidence.
3. **Agreed Scope:** Clear commercial terms and scope are agreed upfront (`https://www.reviewell.com/pricing`).
4. **Casework:** Reviewell prepares the structured evidentiary record and submits through appropriate platform and legal/privacy routes.
5. **Follow-up:** The client tracks progress in the Reviewell workspace (`https://www.reviewell.com/dashboard`) until platform resolution.
